title: The K-th Symbol of the Growing Row

concept.title: The symbol at the position k is the parity of the number of 1-bits in k - 1
body: Build rows of 0s and 1s. The row 1 is `0`. To get the next row, replace every `0` by `01` and every `1` by `10`. The rows are `0`, `01`, `0110`, `01101001`, and so on; the row `n` has `2^(n-1)` symbols. For a question `n k` print the **k-th symbol of the row `n`** (counting from 1). For `n = 4` and `k = 5` the row is `01101001` and the answer is 1. The row `60` has more than 5 * 10^17 symbols, so we cannot build it.

Follow one symbol upwards. The symbol at the position `k` of the row `n` comes from the symbol at the position `ceil(k / 2)` of the row `n - 1`: it is the **first** child (the same symbol) when `k` is odd, and the **second** child (the opposite symbol) when `k` is even. So going from the position `k` up to the first row, we flip the answer every time `k` is even. In the first row the symbol is 0.

body.code:
flips = 0
while k > 1:
    if k % 2 == 0:             # the second child is the opposite of its parent
        flips ^= 1
    k = (k + 1) // 2           # the position of the parent in the row above
print(flips)

body: A closer look gives a formula: the sequence of the symbols is the famous *Thue–Morse sequence*, in which the symbol at the (0-based) position `i` is the **parity of the number of 1-bits of `i`**. So the answer is `popcount(k - 1) % 2` and the row number does not matter at all. For `k = 5`: `k - 1 = 4 = 100`, popcount 1, answer 1. This works in O(1) with a popcount.

statement: Rows of symbols are built as follows: the row 1 is `0`; each next row is obtained by replacing every `0` of the previous row by `01` and every `1` by `10`. For each question `n k` print the k-th symbol (counting from 1) of the row `n`.
inputFormat: The first line has `q`: the number of questions.
Each of the next `q` lines has two numbers `n` and `k`.
outputFormat: Print `q` symbols on one line, separated by spaces.

examples.note: Row 1: 0; row 2: 01; row 4: 01101001, its 5th symbol is 1. The answers are 0 0 1 1.

hints: Write a few rows and look at the pattern.
The k-th symbol of a row is the k-th symbol of any longer row (the rows are prefixes of each other).
It equals the parity of the number of ones in the binary notation of k - 1.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

q = int(input())
qs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

explanation: The rows are prefixes of one Thue–Morse sequence, in which the symbol at the 0-based position i is the parity of popcount(i); so the answer is popcount(k - 1) mod 2.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

q = int(input())
qs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

out = []
for row, k in qs:
    out.append(bin(k - 1).count("1") % 2)
print(*out)
